cases.sentence: Еще Бетси не успела выйти из залы, как Степан Аркадьич, только что приехавший от Елисеева, где были получены ___, встретил ее в дверях.
cases.explain: «свежие устрицы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Before Betsy had time to walk out of the drawing-room, she was met in the doorway by Stepan Arkadyevitch, who had just come from Yeliseev’s, where a consignment of fresh oysters had been received.

cases.sentence: – А! княгиня! вот ___! – заговорил он. – А я был у вас.
cases.explain: «приятная встреча» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah! princess! what a delightful meeting!” he began. “I’ve been to see you.”

cases.sentence: Ни за что я так не благодарен возвращению ___, как за целованье рук. – Он поцеловал руку Бетси. – Когда же увидимся?
cases.explain: «старинных мод» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Don’t put on your glove yet, princess; let me kiss your hand. There’s nothing I’m so thankful to the revival of the old fashions for as the kissing the hand.” He kissed Betsy’s hand. “When shall we see each other?”

cases.sentence: Я не только устраиваю свои, но и чужие ___, – сказал он с значительным выражением лица.
cases.explain: «семейные дела» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Oh, yes, I deserve a great deal, for I’ve become a most serious person. I don’t only manage my own affairs, but other people’s too,” he said, with a significant expression.

cases.sentence: Я не только устраиваю свои, но и чужие семейные дела, – сказал он с ___ лица.
cases.explain: «значительным выражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Oh, yes, I deserve a great deal, for I’ve become a most serious person. I don’t only manage my own affairs, but other people’s too,” he said, with a significant expression.

cases.sentence: – Весь город об этом говорит, – сказала она. – Это ___.
cases.explain: «невозможное положение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The whole town’s talking of it,” she said. “It’s an impossible position. She pines and pines away. He doesn’t understand that she’s one of those women who can’t trifle with their feelings. One of two things: either let him take her away, act with energy, or give her a divorce. This is stifling her.”

cases.sentence: Я была несчастлива и думала, что нельзя быть несчастнее, но того ___, которое теперь испытываю, я не могла себе представить.
cases.explain: «ужасного состояния» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I have heard it said that women love men even for their vices,” Anna began suddenly, “but I hate him for his virtues. I can’t live with him. Do you understand? the sight of him has a physical effect on me, it makes me beside myself. I can’t, I can’t live with him. What am I to do? I have been unhappy, and used to think one couldn’t be more unhappy, but the awful state of things I am going through now, I could never have conceived. Would you believe it, that knowing he’s a good man, a splendid man, that I’m not worth his little finger, still I hate him. I hate him for his generosity. And there’s nothing left for me but. …”

cases.sentence: Его тихие ___ и улыбки действовали смягчающе успокоительно, как миндальное масло.
cases.explain: «успокоительные речи» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: And Stepan Arkadyevitch smiled. No one else in Stepan Arkadyevitch’s place, having to do with such despair, would have ventured to smile (the smile would have seemed brutal); but in his smile there was so much of sweetness and almost feminine tenderness that his smile did not wound, but softened and soothed. His gentle, soothing words and smiles were as soothing and softening as almond oil. And Anna soon felt this.

cases.sentence: Его тихие успокоительные речи и улыбки действовали смягчающе успокоительно, как ___.
cases.explain: «миндальное масло» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: And Stepan Arkadyevitch smiled. No one else in Stepan Arkadyevitch’s place, having to do with such despair, would have ventured to smile (the smile would have seemed brutal); but in his smile there was so much of sweetness and almost feminine tenderness that his smile did not wound, but softened and soothed. His gentle, soothing words and smiles were as soothing and softening as almond oil. And Anna soon felt this.

cases.explain: «натянутая струна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No, Stiva,” she said, “I’m lost, lost! worse than lost! I can’t say yet that all is over; on the contrary, I feel that it’s not over. I’m an overstrained string that must snap. But it’s not ended yet … and it will have a fearful end.”

cases.sentence: Опять он понял по ее ___, что этот один выход, по ее мнению, есть смерть, и он не дал ей договорить.
cases.explain: «испуганному взгляду» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Again he knew from her terrified eyes that this one way of escape in her thought was death, and he would not let her say it.

cases.explain: «Ужасная ошибка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Анна задумчивыми ___ посмотрела на него и ничего не сказала.
cases.explain: «блестящими глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Anna looked at him with dreamy, shining eyes, and said nothing.
